text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPEN — high tail latency observed on dedicated pool us-east-1 (gp-dedicated-45). Severity: P1. Paging oncall.

sam: got the page, on it. seeing p95 jump and p99 rocket — digging into metrics now.

anya: quick summary from runtime: sudden influx of short streaming sessions (~150k/min) from a single customer cohort. pool gp-dedicated-45 saturated, queue depth peaked ~2400. warmup queue is long, hot-start slots exhausted. streaming stalls reported (clients get initial tokens then stall).

maria: support: MuseCorp SLA contact says ~30% of their streaming sessions experienced stalls/timeouts starting ~10:08 UTC. They're on Dedicated and using our streaming API heavily. They want ETA.

sam: metric snapshot:
```
p95_latency: 420ms (baseline ~120ms)
p99_latency: 3.2s (baseline ~450ms)
queue_depth: 2400
free_slots: 0
autoscaler_lag: 35s (requests to provision nodes queued)
streams_in_progress: +80% over baseline
```

anya: autoscaler logs show scale requests being throttled by cloud provider in the warmup path (rate limit on instance launches). also seeing slot registration delay ~60-90s which pushes requests into queue. warmup concurrency + model KV cache miss rate high (many short sessions -> cold KV use).

sam: initial mitigation applied: 1) throttled incoming low-priority routes to reduce queue pressure, 2) manual scale command executed to request +4 slots while autoscaler recovers, 3) enabled fallback model for non-critical traffic.

anya: applied command:
```
# manual bump
redwood ctl pools scale --pool gp-dedicated-45 --add-slots 4 --reason "incident 1759999999 manual bump"
```
logs: some instances accepted, others pending due to cloud rate-limit errors (429).

david: product: we should proactively notify top impacted customers. Maria, can you send a short holding message to MuseCorp? say we're mitigating and will follow up with root cause.

maria: yes, sending now. short note: "We're seeing increased queueing on your Dedicated pool causing streaming stalls. Mitigations in progress; we'll follow up with timeline & root cause." :white_check_mark:

sam: triage notes: root cause appears to be combination of (A) burst of many short-lived streaming sessions that defeat KV caching and force repeated warmups, (B) cloud provider instance launch throttling causing autoscaler lag, (C) pool sizing config had conservative warmup concurrency causing slot registration bottleneck.

infra-bot: cloud events: 2024-11-07T10:07:52Z - compute API rate limit exceeded for region us-east-1, subsequent requests queued.

anya: short-term mitigations proposal (apply now):
- divert low-priority and non-paying customer traffic to separate warm pool (gp-warm-1)
- increase pool slot prewarm concurrency to reduce per-slot registration time (temp config)
- reduce handshake/warmup timeout to prioritize fast failures for small sessions
- keep manual scale until autoscaler steady-state > 5m

sam: executed divert for 3 low-priority routes. monitoring queue depth. p95 moving down marginally (from 420ms -> 300ms). p99 still high due to stalled streams.

anya: also enabling model fallback for streaming: route short sessions to smaller quantized variant (base-quant-v2) to speed token throughput. this will reduce accuracy slightly but improves tail.

sam: customer impact assessment so far: MuseCorp ~30% affected, some other customers (2 mid-market) seeing degraded streaming (10-15% fail rate). no full data-plane outages; mainly increased latency and streaming stalls.

david: escalation decision? do we need cross-team paging to cloud provider ops / account team?

anya: yes, recommend we open provider support ticket for accelerated quota and request deeper look at rate-limits. I'll include logs showing throttled launches.

sam: runtime workaround timeline: manual +4 slots applied at 10:18 UTC; diverted low-priority traffic at 10:22 UTC; model fallback enabled 10:27 UTC. p95 improved to ~200-260ms post-mitigations; p99 still ~1.5-2.0s.

oncall-l4: taking over active coordination. sam — handoff summary received. my actions: 1) keep manual scale until autoscaler recovers, 2) maintain route diverts, 3) coordinate provider ticket and increase escalation if >30m to steady state, 4) prepare rollback plan if fallback causes unacceptable quality regression for paying customers.

maria: outreach: MuseCorp on conference call, they've acknowledged mitigations and requested ETA for root cause & post-incident report.

infra-bot: provider ticket opened: INC-8472 (compute rate limit) — requesting quota bump & backfill of failed launch attempts. ticket link: https://cloud.vendor/ticket/INC-8472 (internal).

anya: temporary config change applied: increased prewarm_concurrency to 6 for gp-dedicated-45. monitor for memory/cpu pressure.

sam: monitoring: queue_depth trending down to ~600 over last 10m, stream success rate improving. setting page to resolved when p99 < 800ms for 10m sustained.

oncall-l4: ack. I'll stay on the thread and coordinate customer comms + postmortem owner assignment. tagging @postmortem.

maria: MuseCorp update: they want a writeup; please include timeline & mitigations. assigning follow-up to David for customer-facing report.

sam: short-term status: mitigations stabilizing system. root cause hypothesis stands. next steps: keep autoscaler manual bump for 15-30m, await provider response, collect traces for KV cache churn, prepare postmortem.

oncall-l4: handing to day SRE rotation at 11:00 UTC unless further regression. will update incident channel if anything changes. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status: mitigated (engineering mitigations applied). monitoring. will convert to postmortem task if root cause confirmed.
